title: Chapter 11 — Rigging Season
description: Mr. Adjust offers fifteen percent. Funke draws a line. The motor park boils over. And there is always a flight to London.

beats.headline: POLL: IT IS CLOSE
beats.text: Our scientific poll of the people at Baba Radio's stall shows {stat:votes} percent for the Teacher, and the rest for "Honourable Owó Ńlá or anybody with rice". Margin of error: plenty.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A man in a beige safari suit is waiting in your office. He has a laminated ID card on a lanyard and the calm of a man who has done this before.

beats.speaker: mrAdjust
beats.text: Good afternoon, sir. I am from the commission. Logistics. (He pronounces it lo-GIS-tics.) Let us say there are... fluctuations, on election night. Fifteen percent can fluctuate in your direction.

beats.speaker: mrAdjust
beats.text: ₦300,000. Half now, half when the figures settle. Very affordable democracy, sir.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: (Quietly, by the door.) Teacher. Owó Ńlá has already paid him. If you don't, those fifteen percent go to the other side.

variants.text: (Quietly, by the door.) Teacher. You told me you were staying honest. I am just telling you: Owó Ńlá has already paid him.

beats.speaker: mrAdjust
beats.text: He is holding out a pen. It is a nice pen.

options.text: Keep him talking while your phone records. (For Ifeoma.)
options.lockedText: You would need somebody to send it to

beats.speaker: mrAdjust
beats.text: ...and the collation centre is where we do the real work, sir. Ward 4, 7 and 9 are already settled. (He has no idea. He is enjoying explaining.)

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: Seyi told me about the man in the safari suit.

variants.text: Seyi told me you paid the man in the safari suit. (She is holding a packed bag. Hers.)

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: If you do this, you do it without me. I will not stand on a podium and clap for stolen votes.

options.text: "Then I will undo it. I will get the money back."
"Funke, this is how it works. You will thank me when we win."

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: (She hugs you, which she has not done since the rice.) Thank God. I was ready to leave. I had even packed. (She shows you the bag. It is full of your shirts. "I was going to make you leave," she says.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Saturday. Your last rally at the motor park. Halfway through your speech, somebody throws a bottle. Then a chair. Then the crowd is not a crowd, it is a river, and it is coming for the stage.

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: TEACHER! RUN! This one is not politics, this one is physics!

caught.toast: They tore your agbada. A danfo driver hid you under the seat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Night. A text from Baba Oko's number: "Owó Ńlá has withdrawn. You are now my only horse. Do not disappoint me." Another text, from an unknown number: "Your file is at the EFCC. Baba Oko sent it. Insurance."

beats.speaker: seyi
beats.text: Teacher... there is a flight to London on Thursday. "Medical tourism". Many great men have had very long medical treatments. You will come back when it is calm.

options.text: "I am staying. Election Day is mine."

beats.title: Rigging Season
beats.summary: Everyone has shown you their price. Now you have to show them yours.
